findings.heading: Package errors
findings.proposition: English gives the remedy for the masked select(): write dplyr:: explicitly, or re-order package loading so that dplyr is loaded after all the others. The Turkish sentence folds both remedies into the agent of the masking clause ('masked by MASS::select(), by the one specifying dplyr:: or re-ordering your package for dplyr'), so no remedy is stated.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader learns that select() was masked but is never told what to do about it, and in particular never learns that dplyr must be loaded last.

findings.heading: Factor errors
findings.proposition: The comment line names the value being added to the factor. English names it "Missing", matching the replace_na(age_cat, "Missing") call shown two lines below. Turkish names it "Eksik", which appears nowhere in the code beside it.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot connect the described value to the replace_na() call in the same block, and may believe the string literal in the call is localised when it is not.

findings.heading: Typo errors
findings.proposition: The prose tells the reader which literal string to look for in the error. English says look for "unexpected symbol", which is exactly the text in the block above it. Turkish says look for "Beklenmeyen simge", a string R never emits and which does not appear in the block above it.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader scans real R output for a Turkish phrase that never occurs, and does not recognise the English 'unexpected symbol' message as the one meant.

findings.heading: Function syntax errors
findings.proposition: The leading comment states the cause of the error. English: recode() was run WITHOUT re-stating the x variable inside mutate(x = recode(x, OLD = NEW)). Turkish turns it into an instruction: 'repeat the code in order to re-state the x variable in mutate(x = recode(x, OLD = NEW))'.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader takes the comment as a fix to apply rather than as the mistake that produced the error, so the diagnosis of the following error message is lost.

findings.heading: Factor errors
findings.proposition: The comment describes an action already taken. English: 'Tried to add a value to a factor'. Turkish uses the imperative 'eklemeye çalışın' ('try to add a value to a factor'), an instruction to the reader.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader reads the line as a step to perform instead of the mistake that generated the invalid-factor-level error below it.

findings.heading: Factor errors
findings.proposition: The line reproduces R's verbatim error output. English shows 'Problem with `mutate()` input `age_cat`.' Turkish replaces it with a Turkish sentence, "'age_cat' girişi 'mutate()' ile ilgili sorun olur.", presenting as R output text that R does not emit. The two lines below it in the same block remain in English.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader does not recognise the real English error message when it appears in their console, and cannot search for it verbatim.

findings.heading: R Markdown errors
findings.proposition: English states a prohibition: use out.width= or out.height= and *not* fig.width= and fig.height=. The Turkish sentence stops at 'kontrol edin' and leaves the rest as a fragment in which the emphasised word 'not' is untranslated; in Turkish 'not' means 'note', so the prohibition is not conveyed.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader may read the fragment as 'also note fig.width= and fig.height=' and keep using the very options that cause the error.

findings.heading: Plotting errors
findings.proposition: The illustrated scale_fill_manual() call uses R colour literals. English shows c("orange", "purple"). Turkish shows c("turuncu", "mor"), which are not R colour names and would raise an invalid colour name error.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader copying the illustrated values gets an invalid-colour error instead of the insufficient-values error the section is about.

findings.heading: Miscellaneous
findings.proposition: English tells the reader to check the pipes (%>%) between re-arranged dplyr verbs. Turkish renders 'piped' as 'Tünellenmiş' ('tunnelled') and 'pipe' as 'tünel' ('tunnel'), so the text refers to a tunnel in the middle and a tunnel at the end, which the English does not support and which has no referent in R.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot tell that the advice is about a missing or leftover %>% operator, so the single check this section offers is unusable.

findings.heading: Interpreting error messages
findings.proposition: English links the Getting help page as [Getting help](help.qmd). Turkish writes [Yardım alma] with no link target, so the cross-reference to that chapter is absent.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is told to see a page on getting help but is given no way to reach it, and the text renders as literal brackets.

findings.heading: Common errors
findings.proposition: English links Noam Ross's analysis at .../blob/master/misc/stack-overflow-common-r-errors.md. In Turkish the URL is cut after '/misc' and the remaining path fragment '/stack-overflow-common-r-errors.md' is left in the running text, so the link does not point at the analysis.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader following the link lands on a directory rather than the cited analysis of common R error messages.

findings.heading: Resources
findings.proposition: English links the r-bloggers post as a single markdown link. In Turkish the closing bracket and the opening parenthesis are separated by intervening words, so the markdown link is broken and the resource is not hyperlinked.
findings.reader_consequence: The only resource in the chapter renders as bracketed text plus a bare URL, so the reader cannot click through to it.

findings.heading: Package errors
findings.proposition: English gives three causes for 'could not find function': a typo, forgetting to install the package, or forgetting to load it. Turkish gives a typo and a single 'yüklemeyi unuttuğunuz', collapsing install and load into one verb.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader whose package is installed but not attached with library() is not pointed at the loading step as a separate cause.
